historical_references.context: Thamir ibn Amr al-Majishu was a notable poet and leader from the Banu Hanifah tribe in pre-Islamic Arabia. He is best known for his poem 'Al-Sharh al-Kabeer' in which he criticized the idolatry of his people and urged them to abandon it. He is also said to have encouraged the Arab tribes to unite under one king, which ultimately led to the rise of the powerful pre-Islamic confederacy known as the 'Axomites' or 'Aws and Khazraj'.

historical_references.context: Thamir ibn Qais is mentioned in Ibn Hazm's work as a famous poet from the Banu Sabah tribe. He is said to have been a contemporary of the early Islamic caliphs 'Umar ibn Al-Khattab and 'Uthman ibn Affan. Thamir's poetry is known for its eloquence and depth, and he is considered one of the major figures in the development of Arabic poetry during the Islamic Golden Age.
